bio: I'm a software engineer in Bangalore, studying Information Science at UVCE. I like problems where code has to touch the physical world: a servo that has to move on time, a model that has to fit on a Jetson, a voice agent that has to hold up on a real phone call.

Right now I'm an AI and software engineering intern at Hoogway.ai, working on a production voice-AI pipeline, and I'm joining Dell in June 2027. Outside of work I build robots, train a reinforcement-learning environment on a tendon-driven arm in MuJoCo, and rebuild language-model pieces from scratch to see how they work.

now.title: Now
now.text: AI and software engineering intern at Hoogway.ai, on a production voice-AI pipeline. Joining Dell in June 2027. On the side: training an RL environment on SpiRobs, a three-tendon arm simulated in MuJoCo.

work.intro: I work on a production, real-time voice AI pipeline: the prompts it runs, the audio it records and the tools the team uses to review calls.

items.title: A prompt system that improves itself
text: Live call traffic is routed across 4 competing prompt variants using Thompson Sampling and Bayesian selection. An automated scorer grades every call on five rubrics: clarity, task completion, engagement, accuracy and tone.

An A/B and regeneration framework retires the losers and writes new variants by distilling traits from the survivors. It replaced ad-hoc prompt tweaking with a statistically sound decision loop, wired into the voice pipeline, LLM APIs and call transcripts. I also fixed prompt-attribution mismatches in the bandit, so it only learns from correctly attributed data.

items.title: Audio infrastructure at scale
text: I reverse-engineered a third-party telephony provider's recording-access protocol and built a server-side audio proxy with HTTP Range forwarding and multi-credential fallback.

To find dead recordings without downloading them, I wrote a pure-Python MP3 duration engine that reads raw MPEG frame headers. It gets exact length (±0.07s) from only the first 16KB of a file. Run asynchronously over 27K recordings, it filtered out silent and sub-3-second audio and cut projected bandwidth from about 4GB to a fraction of that.

The data side is a multi-tenant pipeline that streams and serializes a 90K+ document MongoDB corpus without loading it into memory. Along the way I closed silent data-corruption risks in the ingest path.

items.title: Call review platform
text: A self-contained full-stack tool for reviewing calls: audio player, structured forms that auto-save, live analytics and a deterministic assignment algorithm that guarantees no two reviewers get the same call. FastAPI, vanilla JS and SQLite, packaged with Docker and deployed on Linux.

projects.title: SpiRobs
projects.kind: MuJoCo simulation and RL environment · personal project
summary: A 3D simulation in MuJoCo of a tendon-driven robotic arm: three tendons, three actuators. I'm training a reinforcement-learning environment on it, and training is going well.

projects.title: Sesame
summary: Sesame is an open-source conversational robot designed by Dorian Todd. I rebuilt it on my own electronics instead of the original PCB, then wrote the firmware that ties everything together.

A single ESP32 handles the microphone, speaker, display and eight servos. It listens for voice commands, talks back and moves in response. I also edited the enclosure's top-cover STL so the new electronics fit.
specs: Microphone and speaker, hands-free voice I/O

projects.title: Edge AI and robotics
summary: Real-time object detection running on-device, where compute is tight. An ESP32 turns the model's output into physical action, so the robot sees something and reacts to it.
specs: ESP32 bridging model output to actuators

projects.title: Mars Surface Survey UAV
summary: A drone built for an ISRO-organized hackathon that simulated autonomous surveying of the Martian surface. I worked on software and electronics subsystems and on integrating them on the aerial platform under competition constraints.

projects.title: GPT-2 transformer
summary: A mini GPT-2 written from the ground up: custom tokenizer, token and positional embeddings, causal multi-head self-attention, residual feed-forward layers and autoregressive generation. Trained on Tiny Shakespeare.

projects.title: BPE tokenizer
summary: The cl100k_base tokenizer used by GPT-4, reimplemented from scratch: subword tokenization, merge rules and vocabulary construction.

projects.title: Word2Vec
summary: Word embeddings built without a framework, capturing semantic relationships as the base for similarity and analogy tasks.

projects.title: BrainCells
summary: A neural network built using only raw PyTorch tensors: no torch.nn, no autograd. Forward pass, activations, loss, backprop and weight updates all written by hand.

projects.title: Naive Bayes spam classifier
summary: A spam classifier from scratch using word frequencies and Bayes’ theorem, with no ML libraries.

projects.title: From-scratch implementations
summary: Perceptron, softmax regression, Gaussian discriminant analysis and SGD, written with only NumPy and the math, a repo I keep adding to.

ESP32 (WROOM, CAM), Raspberry Pi 4/5, NVIDIA Jetson Nano, STM32, I²C, PWM, servo and actuator control, PCA9685, power regulation, edge AI
PyTorch, TensorFlow, Keras, Hugging Face Transformers, NumPy, scikit-learn, OpenCV, LangChain. Deep learning, NLP, LLMs, computer vision, Bayesian methods, multi-armed bandits, prompt engineering.
Linux, Git, Docker, FastAPI, REST APIs, MongoDB, SQLite, async and concurrent programming
